layer_note: Nondi's limping song is first-person report, so the knows-by field is dense with direct experience. Its breath layer is mostly named (மூலாதாரம், மணிபூரகம், விசுத்தி, நாசிமுனை, ஒன்பது வாசல்) and so not a cipher; keys are needed for the triangle, the three flames, the great path and the rasa drink. The alchemy layer holds the one plain claim in the pilot of a pill that gives flight (2305), recorded as a claim.

literal.reading: Bowing daily to the feet of Ambika, the first Parapara who is Sivasakti, and taking refuge in the flower-feet of the elephant of the triangle in the faultless flame-light.

breath.reading: The elephant of the triangle is Ganapati seated at the triangle of the root centre: the invocation is already a map of the body, the Mother and then the lord of the root.

literal.reading: The roll of siddhas begins: Tirumular, Kalangi, Bogar, Agastya of Pothigai, Dhanvantari, Karuvurar, Idaikkadar, Atri, Kalaikkodar, Macchamuni, Pulathiyar.
The roll continues with Sundaranandar, Kapilar, Konganar, Sutamuni, Kosikar, Vedamuni, Nandisar and Sattaimuni, whom the poet worshipped.
Knowing the door of the five senses, discerning the true way of the Brahma mantra and parting from agitation, he bowed resolutely at the siddhas' feet.

breath.reading: Knowing the door of the senses is knowing how to shut it: the withdrawal that precedes the practice.

literal.reading: Leaving chariyai and kiriyai, and touching beyond them the foot of the great yoga that is the means, the transcendent appeared; is it in my power to tell what it was to simply remain?

breath.reading: Yoga is the means beyond the rites.

consciousness.reading: 'Simply remaining' is the state past effort, and it cannot be told.

social.reading: Temple worship and rite are left behind.

literal.reading: Taking hold of the Parapara space with the mind made one, seeing the arising of supreme consciousness, he drank fittingly the undeparting nectar of bliss, the ancient thing without support. The syntax is loose.

consciousness.reading: The supreme space is grasped by a unified mind, and the supportless is tasted as bliss.

literal.reading: I came to know, I knew jnana, I saw in full the form of the endless Parabrahman and broke off attachment to this world.

consciousness.reading: The endless Brahman seen whole; attachment ends with the seeing.

literal.reading: When the pure supreme space appeared as light I gained the joy of true knowledge; beholding Being, Consciousness and Bliss, that all is Brahman is hard to tell.

consciousness.reading: The Advaitic formula, all is Brahman, given as what was seen in the space become light.

literal.reading: In the supreme space, the light between the eyes shining at the middle of the nose-tip, I beheld the teacher's holy dance and touched the state of silence.

breath.reading: The gaze fixed at the nose-tip and between the eyes, the classical yogic fixation, named plainly.

literal.reading: Becoming clear that thought is dream, forgetting even that thought, forgetting the rising kalai, forgetting the self that says 'mine', and renouncing the part that does not churn in the pure sea (obscure).

breath.reading: எழுகலை as the rising phases of the breath (or the moon's digits) let go.

consciousness.reading: A chain of forgettings: thought, the knowledge that thought is dream, and the self that says 'mine'.

literal.reading: Having seen in truth what the pranava Om is, I gained great good; leaving the ego that says 'we', I knew my aim.

consciousness.reading: Knowing Om and leaving the ego go together.

literal.reading: Leaving desire, given the strength to cut off the five senses that run out, crossing the bond and walking exactly as the guru's word said.
Taking the pill of flight (கவனக் for கமனக்) and going by it deep along the sky path, I went to Sathuragiri, where the great siddhas of austerity live, and rejoiced.

breath.reading: The pill as the retained breath or seed and the sky path as the inner sky: the journey would be in the body.

alchemy.reading: The siddha tradition's claim that a pill gives travel through the air, made here in the first person; the verse names no ingredient and no preparation, and it is recorded as a claim.

literal.reading: With the nine siddhas of supreme knowledge who sit on the rock of austerity, I knew the form of Siva, and seeing the lamp-light in my mind I broke off longing.

consciousness.reading: A light seen in the mind ends longing.

literal.reading: I knew the root support and rejoiced to see the lamp-light of the three flames; I learned the manifold arts, and by the grace of my grandfather Nandisar I was glad.

breath.reading: The root centre is named; the three flames are the sun, moon and fire of the body, the two breaths and the root fire.

literal.reading: Knowing the experience of yoga, I saw that the manipuraka is a great attainment for the best, and that remaining in the vishuddhi state so as not to die, one's own state there becomes the good state.

breath.reading: Two of the six centres are named and given their fruits; the throat centre carries deathlessness.

literal.reading: I stood at what I saw; knowing that Sivasakti was imagination, I rejoiced and went beyond; seeing the path once granted to mother Uma, I drank the intoxication of the rasa drink.

breath.reading: The rasa drink as the nectar that falls from the moon in the head.

alchemy.reading: ரசபானம் as the mercury preparation the alchemist siddhas claim to drink; the verse gives no more than the word and its intoxication.

consciousness.reading: The vision of Sivasakti is itself a construct, to be passed beyond.

literal.reading: Having seen the wonder of the fullness that none can know, my speech subsided; by the grace of the goddess Manonmani I knew it and merged in it.

consciousness.reading: Silence comes as the effect of seeing the fullness, not as a discipline.

literal.reading: Day by day I saw and knew the place beyond desire; I took the name 'she is Vami', which sages and gods praise, and rose in the Supreme.

consciousness.reading: The place past desire is the state itself.

literal.reading: Seeing the state called the silence at the end of nada, I stayed there, losing sleep and food; I knew the way of Vedanta and, crossing the house of ignorance, saw the higher house.

breath.reading: The end of the inner sound, with sleep and food lost, as the yogi's signs.

consciousness.reading: The final silence lies where sound ends.

literal.reading: I read many sastras, forgot the company of wicked chandalas, learned to know the worthy vessel, and joining with devotion those (worthy) ones I saw release.

social.reading: The caste word சண்டாளர் is used as abuse for wicked company: the verse uses caste vocabulary as a moral insult rather than criticising caste.

literal.reading: This salted pot of a body came the way it came; people who do not know the truth call it good, and like copper-workers (செப்புக் குயமானார், obscure) wander the land in desire and churn in bondage.

alchemy.reading: If செப்புக் குயமானார் means those who work copper, the line is a dig at alchemists chasing gold from base metal and wandering in desire.

literal.reading: Certain that this body, an unstable false cage, has no substance, I went in fear to a mountain cave, learned the way of Sivajnana and became straight in it.
I lowered myself as 'the knowing lame one'; I knew the fitting state and the clarity of the form of Parabrahman that the guru told. The unit lacks its first line.

consciousness.reading: Self-abasement as the destruction of ego, under the section heading.

literal.reading: I realised myself by myself, realised the eight places and the nine gates, then shut those doors, and going through the great high path I reached the holy.

breath.reading: The nine gates are shut (the senses withdrawn) and the great path is the central channel to the crown.

consciousness.reading: The self is known by itself first.

links.note: Both put the goal beyond the first two paths: Arunagiri's supreme light cannot be reached by those joined to chariyai and kiriyai, and Nondi leaves them to touch the foot of yoga and finds a state he cannot tell.

Both set aside chariyai and kiriyai: Agappei says chariyai will not do though it gives salokam, and kiriyai gains nothing; Nondi leaves both and touches yoga as the means beyond them. They agree on the two rungs of rite and part on the third: Nondi makes yoga the way, while Agappei (in 1676, outside this pilot) denies yoga too.

Both place the Lord at a point measured from the nose-tip and beyond speech: Tirumular puts his dwelling a few finger-breadths from it, which the Veda shrinks from telling; Nondi sees the teacher's dance in the light between the eyes at the nose-tip and falls into silence.

Before the key, Nondi sees 'the lamp-light of the three flames' after knowing the root support, and Agappei lists 'the unchanging mandalas, three' after the Agamas' tattvas. Under the three-lights key both are the sun, moon and fire of the body. Nondi needs the key less (flames at the root suggest it), Agappei more (he names only three mandalas). With the key, Nondi reports seeing what Agappei lists and, in 1660, sets aside.

Both promise that yoga at a named place keeps the body from death: Tirumular, fixing the mind twelve finger-breadths below the nose, says the body never decays; Nondi says that staying in the vishuddhi state is 'so as not to die'. Both are plain claims of bodily deathlessness from practice, and neither needs a key; Thiruppugazh 355 rejects the same aim.

Nondi values the throat centre as the way 'not to die' (சாகாதிருந்திட); Arunagirinathar asks not to become the foolish yogi who, thinking this impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath at the nostrils and withers eating herbs. The conflict is over yoga used to keep the body, and it holds if Nondi's deathlessness is bodily; it dissolves if சாகா means the state beyond death rather than an undying body.

The alchemist's pill (குளிகை) in both. Tirumular makes the five syllables the pill that turns the body's cage to gold, an internalised alchemy; Nondi, on the plain reading, claims a pill that carried him through the air to Sathuragiri. The pairing shows the same object taken inward by the older text and outward, as a physical claim, by the later one.

Both credit the goddess Manonmani with giving the means: in Tirumular she wakes the sleeping yogi and gives the upaya; in Nondi it is by her grace that he knew the unknowable fullness and merged in it.

Idaikkadar orders silence as a discipline: stay like an owl and achieve silence (மோனத்தைச் சாதி). Nondi reports silence as an effect: having seen the wonder of the fullness, my speech subsided (பேச்சடங்கினேன்). Nondi qualifies the command: silence achieved and silence that comes after seeing are not the same, and the second does not wait on the first.

Idaikkadar says Shakti and the Supreme are blended within and are seen there in nishta, which is the goal he names; Nondi says he saw Sivasakti there, knew it was imagination (கற்பனை) and went beyond. The conflict is over whether the inner Shakti-Siva pair is final or a construct to pass; it holds on reading 1862 as the end of the way, and dissolves if Idaikkadar's seeing is a stage. It is also a stance difference (see findings).

The nine gates shut. In Tirumular they all shut together at death, the pandal comes apart and the mourners leave; Nondi, having realised the nine gates, shuts them himself and goes up the great path. The yogi does voluntarily what death does to everyone, which is what the shared figure teaches.

Before the key, Pattinathar calls his body 'a torn rag of four cubits and nine' (நான்முழத்து ஒன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம்), a phrase the flat marks could not construe, and Nondi names the nine gates outright. Under the nine-gates key Pattinathar's nine are the body's nine openings, the tears in the rag. Pattinathar despises the nine-holed body; Nondi closes its nine doors and goes through.

old_links.note: A roll call shares two names with Tirumular's lineage verse; no shared claim.
Consistent rather than qualifying; replaced by 2297 and 1666, which share the act of leaving the rites.
Both put the goal beyond chariyai and kiriyai and call it untellable.
The nose-tip is named in both; holds without a key.
A means that dissolves at the end does not contradict a means that helped; the note supplied its own dissolution.
Only the mountain Sathuragiri is shared.
Manonmani gives the means in both.
Silence at the end of sound in both.
Read a stock caste insult (பொல்லாச் சண்டாளர்) as a doctrine that birth is conduct; the social layer shows the verse uses caste vocabulary, it does not critique it.
The identical உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம் for the body.
The false hut of the body is stock across devotional verse.

Joined two nines that are different things: Nondi's nine gates (openings, shut) and Tirumular's nine nadis (channels, stilled). A number shared is not a key shared. Replaced by Tirumanthiram 152, where the nine gates are the same nine.
Gates closed, then ascent through the central way: named in both; a breath-layer link that needs no key.
Both place the Lord's dance inside the body; heart in 148, brow in 2301.
Nandi to Tirumular to the poet: a lineage stated in the words.
Only the word உற்பனம் is shared; the referents differ.
A fair development within one song.
A body called unstable against a body kept from perishing in nishtai: a real conflict within one poet, and a stance difference (see findings).

source_issues: 2299 and 2316 lack their first line, lifted out as a section heading.
